acceptance_checks: With `sys.path[0] == os.getcwd()`, `modify_sys_path()` removes that first entry.

With an arbitrary value at `sys.path[0]`, the value remains present and in the first position after `modify_sys_path()`, except that separately identified working-directory entries caused by `PYTHONPATH` colon semantics may be removed.
The reported `runpy.run_module("pylint", run_name="__main__", alter_sys=True)` execution does not remove an arbitrary bundled-library entry from the front of `sys.path`.
With an empty `sys.path`, `modify_sys_path()` completes without raising and leaves it empty.
Existing leading-colon and trailing-colon `PYTHONPATH` scenarios continue removing the intended working-directory entries.
When an arbitrary first entry is preserved, leading/trailing-colon cleanup does not remove that entry through positional indexing.
Existing module-execution protection against accidental imports from the current working directory remains covered and passing.
Targeted tests for `modify_sys_path()` and the runpy regression pass.
confirmed_decisions: Initial removal uses exact string matching only: `""`, `"."`, or `os.getcwd()`.
An empty `sys.path` causes no removal and no error.
Every other initial entry is preserved, including the arbitrary bundled-library entry in the reported runpy case.

Leading/trailing-colon `PYTHONPATH` cleanup remains supported and removes only its corresponding working-directory entries, without relying on old indices that could remove a preserved arbitrary entry.
The scope is limited to `modify_sys_path()` and module execution paths that call it; `run_pylint()` and the installed console-script entry point are not broadened to call it.
Regression coverage is contractual for the exact eligible values, arbitrary-first-entry/runpy behavior, empty `sys.path`, and existing `PYTHONPATH` colon cases.
Normalized, resolved, symlinked, or otherwise equivalent spellings of the current working directory are not additionally eligible unless their exact value is `""`, `"."`, or `os.getcwd()`.
summary: Update `modify_sys_path()` so an empty `sys.path` is a no-op; remove `sys.path[0]` only when its exact string value is `""`, `"."`, or `os.getcwd()`; and preserve every other first entry. Retain the existing cleanup for working-directory entries introduced by leading or trailing colons in `PYTHONPATH`, but target those entries so a preserved arbitrary first entry is never removed. Limit the behavioral change to callers of `modify_sys_path()`, including `python -m pylint` and the reported `runpy.run_module(..., run_name="__main__", alter_sys=True)` path; the installed `pylint` console script remains outside this path. Add regression coverage for all three eligible exact values, an arbitrary preserved first entry including the reported runpy scenario, an empty `sys.path`, and existing leading/trailing-colon `PYTHONPATH` behavior. Paths equivalent to the working directory but not exactly equal to one of the three approved strings remain preserved by design.
